edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: ACT changes the pain relationship more than the nociceptive input itself, using acceptance and values-based behavior to reduce disability.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2025 Wang meta analysis in World J Psychiatry, which suggests that acceptance and commitment therapy tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for chronic pain. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
